children: launched the Claude Frontier Academy on Friday with a $100 million commitment to train 10,000 AI engineers by the end of 2027, as the company nears an expected initial public offering (IPO).
The program will draw “frontier deployed engineers” from firms in Anthropic’s Claude Partner Network, according to the company’s press release.

Anthropic said training will begin with a “simulated enterprise deployment” and a graded assessment. Those who pass will enter a residency modeled on medical training, where they will practice on casework before being assessed and credentialed. The company expects the first engineers to be certified in early 2027.
Draup data provided exclusively to CNBC shows job postings for forward deployed engineers and other AI roles have surged in finance this year.
